messages:
anika: Ran a perfetto trace on the client->gateway->runtime path with KV prefetch enabled. Seeing a ~200ms tail bump for a subset of requests starting at T=00:12:34 in the trace. link: https://perfetto.local/trace/1965432100

ben_k: can you paste the timeline snippet? is it during kernel selection or the batching window?

anika: pasted the relevant waterfall:```
Client span  00:12:33.900 - 00:12:34.150
Gateway span 00:12:33.910 - 00:12:34.230
Runtime span 00:12:34.000 - 00:12:34.370  <-- taily
  - KVCACHE PREFETCH start 00:12:34.010
  - kernel_select 00:12:34.050
  - launch kernel (attention) 00:12:34.110
```

flo: interesting that prefetch start is so early but the kernel launch is delayed. any nvprof/nsys correlates?

anika: ran nsys on a repro workload, attaching snippet from the GPU timeline:```
== nsys report ==
cudaLaunchKernel (attention_kernel) queued at 00:12:34.110
cudaStreamWaitEvent for prefetch_event at 00:12:34.105
prefetch memcpy async end at 00:12:34.102
kernel actually starts 00:12:34.200
queued->start latency ~90us (queuing ok) but start delay ~90ms for some launches
```
(Weirdly not all kernels show the 90ms delay, roughly 8% of requests)

samir: 8% tail -> sounds like intermittent handoff bottleneck. Could be stream saturation or a fallback path taking a different queue. Do we have per-request stream ids in the perfetto trace?

anika: yes, I correlated trace event metadata: prefetch uses stream s2, main compute uses s1. When we see the tail, kernel gets moved to s3 in the runtime (we do dynamic stream rebalance) — looks like the runtime's kernel selection path tries to switch to a lower-priority stream when prefetch overlaps.

ben_k: ahah. runtime switch could cause implicit serialization if that stream is currently blocked by a long-running memory copy. Do we have queue depth histograms?

anika: added a histogram of inflight copies per device during the window:```
0-1 copies: 88% of windows
2-3 copies: 9%
>=4 copies: 3% (these map almost exactly to the slow samples)
```

flo: Okay that matches. If prefetches occupy multiple streams and we force kernel to a different low-priority stream, it may be waiting on device-side scheduling. Two options: force kernel onto the same stream as prefetch (risking blocking other kernels) or adjust prefetch concurrency/batching heuristic.

samir: have we checked pinned vs pageable buffer behavior for the prefetch? Pager stalls could look like this.

anika: good call — I re-ran with pinned host buffers for prefetcher, the 90ms spikes disappeared in the perfetto trace sample (tail now within 5ms). nvprof shows memcpy async completes slightly earlier and cudaStreamWaitEvent latency gone.

ben_k: so root cause is prefetch pipeline + stream rebalance + pageable mem copies causing intermittent device-side scheduling delays. Nice find.

flo: for next steps: 1) short-term: change prefetcher to use pinned host buffers in runtime builds for Dedicated. 2) mid-term: update batching heuristic to cap concurrent prefetches to 2 per-device and add a stream affinity policy for compute kernels. 3) add a perfetto annotation in runtime when we do stream rebalance so traces immediately surface this next time.

anika: created a small repro and a draft patch:```
- runtime/prefetcher: use cudaHostAlloc for prefetch buffers when enabled
- runtime/scheduler: add --prefetch-concurrency=2 default
- runtime/tracing: emit event 'stream_rebalance' with target_stream_id
```
PR: https://git.local/redwood/runtime/pull/4321

perfetto-bot: perfetto trace uploaded: https://perfetto.local/trace/1965432100 (annotations added) :white_check_mark:

samir: awesome. I'll review the PR and try a dedicated hardware run tomorrow morning. If that reproduces, we should ship the pinned-buffer change behind a feature flag and monitor token-latency SLOs. :thumbsup:

anika: agreed. i'll add a canary rollout plan and a dashboard tile showing percent >50ms kernel start delay.

ben_k: thanks for the quick triage — great end-to-end use of perfetto + nsys.

flo: bookmarking the trace for follow-up perf postmortem.
